programme: STAT2-driven type I/III interferon-stimulated gene induction: STAT2 transcriptionally activates the core antiviral effector set (OAS1, IFIT2, IFIT3, EIF2AK2/PKR, SAMHD1) and auto-amplifies by inducing IRF9, its own ISGF3 partner — an interferon-response module running without its usual STAT1 co-factor, since STAT1 was stripped out here as tissue-generic to blood/thymus.
role_in_a: In COVID-19, STAT2-dependent ISG induction is the primary cell-intrinsic brake on SARS-CoV-2 replication; loss of this axis (genetic STAT2 deficiency, or its functional equivalent) is a recognized route to severe, poorly-controlled infection.
role_in_b: In thymoma, disordered thymic epithelial selection is expected to generate high-titer autoantibodies against type I interferons — a paraneoplastic phenomenon that would functionally silence the same STAT2/ISGF3 axis systemically, independent of any germline defect.
shared_axis: Both diseases converge on the same failure mode of one pathway — COVID-19 by direct viral pressure on a genetically intact axis, thymoma by autoimmune neutralization of interferon upstream of STAT2 — so a thymoma patient's autoantibody-silenced ISGF3 axis would behave, on SARS-CoV-2 exposure, like a person born with STAT2 deficiency.
reasoning: STAT2 is strongly and specifically placed in COVID-19 (Open Targets percentile 0.98, PMID 42382660 on STAT2-deficient patients with severe viral susceptibility), and thymoma-associated anti-type-I-interferon autoimmunity is separately well established as a class of biology, but nothing in this record states the two together directly — the thymoma-tagged paper here is off-target — so the bridge is built from two independently anchored facts, not a retrieved joint statement. It is also worth noting STAT2 is the weakest-recurring carrying factor considered (26/40), well below ZBTB7B, FOSL2 or NFIL3, so the signal itself is less robust than the top of this list.
support: PMID 42382660 — describes kindreds with autosomal recessive STAT2 deficiency, i.e. loss of this exact axis causing severe susceptibility to viral disease, anchoring role_in_a. PMID 42461263 — describes a STAT2-mutation type I interferonopathy (familial pulmonary alveolar proteinosis), but per the reader's note this is not actually about thymoma, so it supports the STAT2-interferonopathy mechanism in general, not a thymoma-specific claim.
how_to_falsify: Screen a thymoma cohort for neutralizing anti-type-I-interferon autoantibodies, then test patient serum for its ability to block STAT2 phosphorylation and induction of its network targets (OAS1, IFIT2, IFIT3, EIF2AK2) in IFN-alpha-stimulated PBMCs; if autoantibody-positive thymoma serum does not suppress this STAT2 target program, or if autoantibody status does not track with COVID-19 severity in infected thymoma patients, the shared-axis claim fails.
caveats: Blood/thymus tissue pairing across 40 patient-group comparisons from 2 independent cohort pairs. STAT1 and IRF5 were both removed as tissue-generic to blood/thymus, so the fuller ISGF3/interferon-regulatory picture is deliberately truncated to STAT2 alone here — that is a design choice in the input, not an oversight to fill in. KLF9, KLF6 and ZBTB4 were single-view (one patient group only) and are excluded rather than folded into this account. ZBTB7B shows perfect 40/40 recurrence with targets pointing at CD4/CD8 T-lineage biology directly relevant to thymus, but carries zero Open Targets or literature support in either disease in this record, so it is left out of this programme rather than forced in.
